summary: Radar for 2026-11-28, GLP-1 focus. Thanksgiving is over. The two loudest fresh signals both concern semaglutide. (1) Health Canada's NAION vision-loss warning (CBC, Globe and Mail, Yahoo Canada, NOW Toronto, 11-25 to 11-27). It sits on top of the FDA label change from 11-09, so it is peaking, but it's a perfect "label change + felt symptom" search format for our high-CPM Canadian audience. (2) Women's mammogram and breast-density coverage (Newsweek, Fox, 11-26/27). It is observational, so it's only a careful long-video candidate. The best early-stage catches are tirzepatide (Zepbound) in type 1 diabetes, a fresh review picked up by NewsNation on 11-27. It has high search intent but is off-label, so we explain it only, with no insulin advice. The other is the Christmas-dinner felt-symptom wave, which suits Shorts only, since the Thanksgiving long video earned just 194 min. The cancer umbrella review (11-20) plus Targeted Onc (11-27) gives a strong 'does Mounjaro cause cancer?' search video. The gut-bacteria regain story feeds the proven Stopping → Keeping Results series. Retatrutide's TRANSCEND-T2D-2 win over Ozempic is a month old with high competition and heavy gray-market noise, so it only works with a careful fast-turn angle. Evergreen formats that beat the channel's usual views stay at the top for Shorts: hair, nausea, injection site and pen moments. Sequels (After 6 Months, Christmas) must be checked against the live list; never duplicate Foundayo What to Expect, Vial vs Pen, Mounjaro vs Ozempic, Zepbound vs Wegovy or Months 2–6. Rejected: compounded Foundayo 'Melt' chocolate, needle-free tirzepatide patches, 'cheapest tirzepatide online' listings, cut-price/decoy-bust retatrutide, counterfeit-site stories as topics, and celebrity 'how much can I eat' framing. The '53% GI symptoms within 5 years' HCPLive figure could not be verified, so use it only if the primary study is found.

candidates.topic: Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro vision-loss (NAION) warning: Health Canada's new alert plus the FDA label change. Which eye changes need same-day care?
candidates.angle: Calm label explainer for Canadian, US and UK viewers. Sentence 1: 'Health Canada and the FDA now list a very rare eye problem, NAION, for these medicines. Here is what it feels like and what to do.' Cover the felt moment (sudden, painless vision loss in one eye) and how rare it is (label wording 'very rare'). Explain why tirzepatide carries the FDA class labelling too. Say what to do: urgent eye care, and tell your prescriber. No 'stop your medicine' line beyond the label's own wording.
candidates.why_now: Health Canada's warning ran in CBC, Globe and Mail, Yahoo Canada and NOW Toronto between 11-25 and 11-27, two weeks after the FDA label update on 11-09. Search for 'ozempic vision loss' spikes with each wave. Label changes are one of the 10–195× search formats, and our NAION TikTok did 654 views.
